# Run a plan

Commands for this repository. The `orchestration` skill (`orca skills get orchestration`)
holds the general rules of the loop; this skill holds what is specific here. Commands and host
scripts run as your instructions say under Boundaries; read a script's verdict from its log,
not from the exit code Orca reports.

Paths: repo `/Users/serhii/Developer/emdash-images` (REPO), worktree `REPO/.worktrees/emdash-images/<NNN-slug>` (WT),
run folder `/Users/serhii/Developer/emdash-images/.scratch/runs/<NNN-slug>/` (RUN).

## 1. Start

A plan runs in a fresh session of the `architect-run` agent, started with the Orca quick command
«Role: Architect run»: a run makes hundreds of turns, and each re-reads everything said before
it. If this conversation already holds planning or another run, tell the user to start that
session with "run plan NNN" and stop, unless the user says to run here anyway. The run session
knows only the plan, the docs and `status.md`.

1. Grep `.orca-setup.lock.json` for `"rules"`. If it differs from the rules version at the top of
   your instructions, the kit was rendered after this session started and you run on the old
   rules: tell the user to restart you, and dispatch nothing.
   The plan is approved and committed; `git status --porcelain` in REPO prints nothing;
   `./scripts/orca/plan-check.py <plan>` prints `PLAN OK`.
   Check each item of the plan's `Preconditions` with its command or path; a missing one is an
   escalation (section 6), not a task to start around (urbanexteriors plan 001 started before its
   design export existed).
   Run `./scripts/orca/sign-probe.sh`; it must print `SIGN OK`. On `SIGN FAILED` ask the user to
   unlock 1Password now: a locked signer found at the first task commit stops the run after
   the user has left.
2. `orca orchestration run-create --objective "plan NNN" --json`
3. `orca worktree create --name <NNN-slug> --repo path:REPO --base-branch main --setup run --json`
   Always pass `--base-branch main`: Orca's default base can be the remote branch,
   which lacks the unpushed plan commit.
4. Wait for setup: repeat `ls WT/node_modules/.bin/astro` until it exists. Starting a worker earlier
   fails with `terminal_handle_stale`.
5. `orca terminal list --worktree path:WT --json`, then `orca terminal close --terminal <h>` for
   the empty shell and the setup terminal, so only agents remain in WT.
6. Create RUN with `status.md`: run id, worktree, branch, base commit, a task table
   (`| Task | State | Round | Commit | Verdict | Notes |`), and the sections `## Decisions`,
   `## Surprises` and `## Follow-ups for Outcome`. `status.md` is the run's memory: a fresh
   session, the next plan and the user read it, never this conversation.

## 2. Each task

1. Write `RUN/T<n>.spec.md` from `docs/templates/task.md`: the task block from the plan
   verbatim, progress, report and screenshot paths. Take the block with the Read tool (`offset`
   and `limit` from a Grep for `^### T` with `-n` in the plan), not `awk` or `sed`: those ask for
   approval and stop the run until the user answers.
2. `orca orchestration worker-start --spec "Task T<n> of plan NNN. Read the full task spec at <spec path> and follow it exactly." --worktree path:WT --agent codex --json`
   Never pass `--model` or `--effort` for Codex. If it exits non-zero, do not start it again: read
   the receipt's `error.code`, `failedStage` and `residualResources`, follow
   `orca skills get orchestration --reference references/recovery-and-cleanup.md`, and retry only a
   proven `failed` or `stopped` attempt with `worker-start --task <id> --retry-of <dispatch> --worktree path:WT --agent codex --json`.
3. Wait (section 4). Answer `question` messages from the plan, ADRs and docs within the plan's
   scope; anything else is an escalation (section 6). Add every answer to `## Decisions` (task,
   question, answer, why), and every finding the plan did not foresee to `## Surprises`; so does
   a decision the user makes during the run. "Dependencies changed, run install": run
   `orca terminal create --worktree path:WT --title "install" --command "exec ./scripts/orca/install-main.sh <NNN-slug>"`,
   wait for exit, Grep `^INSTALL ` in `WT/.scratch/tmp/install-main.log` and reply with that line
   and the lockfile status; never run the install yourself (it asks the user).
4. On `worker_done`: `worker-release` (it closes the executor's terminal: `processAction`
   `closed_agent_terminal`). A receipt with `retained` and reason `user_takeover` after a
   settled report leaves the idle terminal open even when nobody typed there: close it with
   `orca terminal close --terminal <id>`, note it in `## Surprises`, and do not ask the user.
   Read the report its spec names (`RUN/T<n>.md`, or `RUN/T<n>.fix-<k>.md` in a fix round),
   update `status.md`. A report without a result
   line for each Acceptance item goes back to a fresh executor for the missing evidence before
   any review. A `failed` outcome whose report says "commit waits for
   1Password" left its changes staged in WT. 1Password asks to approve each new executor
   terminal, so a fresh executor would wait for the user again; your terminal was approved by
   the start probe. Commit the staged changes yourself: `cd WT` as its own call, then
   `git commit -m "<the task's message>"` (`git commit --amend -m …` in a fix round) as its own
   call, check `git status --porcelain` is empty, then `cd REPO`. Note it in `## Deviations`. If
   your own commit fails to sign too, escalate (section 6). The review follows as usual.

## 3. Review and fix rounds

1. Write `RUN/T<n>.review-<k>.spec.md` from `docs/templates/review-spec.md`. Ask only for
   commands the reviewer's role runs: it cannot read `.env`, write the database or run host
   scripts, so a check that needs them comes from the executor's report or from you at gates.
   An Acceptance item marked `(gate)` is not the reviewer's: list it as `NOT RUN` with the
   executor's result line and add it to the plan gates you check yourself.
   Write each command plainly, with no `VAR=value` or `env` prefix: Claude Code asks for
   approval on it and the review waits for the user. Put such a setup in a project script.
   Name only paths in WT and RUN: a path in REPO (the amended plan, a doc on `main`)
   stops the reviewer at Claude Code's "read outside the working directories" prompt. When the
   plan was amended during the task, copy the amended lines into the review spec (emdash-images
   plan 017 T1).
2. `./scripts/orca/review.sh start <NNN-slug> T<n> <k>`: it opens a fresh reviewer terminal in
   WT, waits until it is idle and dispatches the review spec. The last line is
   `REVIEW STARTED terminal=<h> dispatch=<id>`; put both in `status.md`. On `REVIEW FAILED <step>`
   read its output; a terminal it names is yours to close.
3. Wait (section 4). Then read `RUN/T<n>.review-<k>.md` and run
   `./scripts/orca/review.sh finish <NNN-slug> <h> <id>`: it releases the dispatch, closes the
   terminal and prints `git -C WT status --porcelain`, which must be
   the same as before the review. The last line must be `REVIEW FINISHED`. `REVIEW FAILED head
   moved` means something the reviewer ran committed into WT: escalate with both hashes.
   Add the review's Notes to `## Follow-ups for Outcome`, and each `NOT RUN` item to the plan
   gates you check yourself at the finish.
4. `VERDICT: PASS`: next task. `VERDICT: FIX`: write `RUN/T<n>.fix-<k>.spec.md` from
   `docs/templates/fix-spec.md` and start a fresh executor with it (section 2, step 2); the
   executor amends its task commit. Then a fresh review. After 3 consecutive FIX verdicts on
   one task, escalate.
5. Every commit that changes code, tests or configuration gets a reviewer's PASS, however small
   (a one-line fix round or a gate fix included). Only a fix round that changes documentation
   alone may be accepted on your own reading of the diff, and only after
   `./scripts/orca/docs-only.sh WT <commit before the fix> <commit after the fix>` prints
   `DOCS ONLY`; put that line in `status.md`. `NOT DOCS ONLY` means a review.

## 4. Waiting and the watchdog

Every turn of yours re-reads your whole context, so an empty wake costs as much as a real one.
Wait only with `./scripts/orca/wait.sh <NNN-slug>`, run in the background; never with a bare
`check --wait` or a `sleep`. It waits on `check --wait` (filtered to `worker_done`, `escalation`
and `question`, so heartbeats never wake you), runs `orca-watch.sh` after each empty check and
`worker-list` after three, and returns within 50 minutes, before your prompt cache expires. Its
first line says why:

- `WAIT MESSAGES`: a batch follows, already marked handled; it is not shown again. Process every
  message in it (answer, release, update `status.md`; a heartbeat needs nothing), then run
  `wait.sh` again. Lost a batch? `orca orchestration inbox --terminal run:<run_id> --limit 50`.
- `WAIT WORKERS`: rows that need action follow, with their `nextAction`. Act on them;
  `unverifiable` liveness is absence of news, never a reason to stop, retry or release a worker.
- `WAIT QUIET`: nothing happened; a watch snapshot follows. Run `wait.sh` again.
- `WAIT ERROR`: an orca call failed; read its output, retry once, then escalate.
- `WAIT ATTENTION`: lines of `orca-watch.sh` start with `ATTENTION` (run it yourself too before
  each review that compares with a reference):
  - approval prompt in a terminal: escalate at once with the terminal title — nobody else sees it;
  - removal failed: rerun `orca worktree rm`;
  - a sleep or wake line since the last check: the Mac slept; wait, do not restart workers.
- A worker that shows no progress: check the sleep lines first; only then treat it as stalled.

## 5. Finish

1. In WT: `orca terminal create --worktree path:WT --title "plan gates" --command "exec ./scripts/orca/plan-gates.sh"`,
   then `orca terminal wait --terminal <h> --for exit --timeout-ms 1800000`, then
   a Grep for `^GATES ` with `-n` in `WT/.scratch/tmp/plan-gates.log`. The last match must be
   `GATES OK`; a failed step goes back to an executor.
3. REPO: `git status --porcelain` prints nothing; `git merge --no-ff task/<NNN-slug>`.
4. If the plan changed `package-lock.json`: `orca terminal create --worktree path:REPO --title "install main" --command "exec ./scripts/orca/install-main.sh"`,
   then `orca terminal wait --terminal <h> --for exit --timeout-ms 900000`, then
   a Grep for `^INSTALL ` with `-n` in `REPO/.scratch/tmp/install-main.log`; the last match must be
   `INSTALL OK`. An install can exit 0 and still leave packages half written; never report
   dependencies as installed without that line.
5. `orca terminal create --worktree path:REPO --title "verify main" --command "exec ./scripts/orca/verify-main.sh NNN"`,
   `orca terminal wait --terminal <h> --for exit --timeout-ms 1200000`, then
   a Grep for `^VERIFY ` with `-n` in `REPO/.scratch/tmp/verify-main.log`; the last match must be
   `VERIFY OK`.
6. `orca orchestration worker-list --run <run> --terminal-state reclaimable --json` returns no
   rows: every settled worker is released. Fill `## Outcome` in the plan, each part of the
   template, from `status.md` and the reviews; under Proposed rules, each finding kind
   (`[defect]`, `[test]`, `[docs]`, …) with the same cause in two or more reviews. Commit it; update `docs/ROADMAP.md`. The next plan learns from
   this Outcome only, so a decision left out of it is lost.
7. `orca terminal create --worktree path:REPO --title "remove worktree" --command "exec ./scripts/orca/remove-worktree.sh <NNN-slug>"`,
   `orca terminal wait --terminal <h> --for exit --timeout-ms 300000`, then
   a Grep for `^REMOVE ` with `-n` in `REPO/.scratch/tmp/remove-worktree.log`; the last match must be
   `REMOVE OK`. The script runs `orca worktree rm --run-hooks` and deletes what Finder's `.DS_Store` writes left behind. On
   `REMOVE FAILED`, ask the user to close Finder windows on the worktree and run it again; never
   report the worktree removed without `REMOVE OK`.
8. Summarise for the user in Ukrainian: tasks, rounds, deviations, follow-ups, proposed
   rules for the user to approve or reject, open questions. Each claim names its evidence: a commit, a verdict, a log line. Then tell the user
   this run session is finished and should be closed; the next plan is planned elsewhere.

## 6. Escalate

For each case your instructions list under "Escalate, do not retry":
`orca worktree set --worktree path:WT --comment "WAITING: <question>"`, put the question first
in your reply, in Ukrainian, and wait.

## 7. Plan amendments

The plan changes only through an escalation (section 6): the user amends it in a planning
session, which commits it in REPO, and tells you "plan amended". Then:

1. `git -C REPO log -1 --format=%H%n%s -- <plan>` shows the amendment commit; read the plan
   from REPO (WT holds the old copy) and its `## Amendments` line; `plan-check.py <plan>` in
   REPO prints `PLAN OK`.
2. Add the amendment to `## Decisions` in `status.md`: commit, tasks changed or added, why.
3. An executor waiting in `ask` for the decision gets the answer "plan amended" with the
   changed lines of its task block (Ownership, Acceptance); Constraints and Change it already
   has stay as they are unless the amendment changed them. A running executor that is not
   waiting is left alone; its review uses the amended block. A task not yet started gets its
   spec from the new version; new tasks run after the existing ones. Done tasks do not change.
4. The Outcome's Deviations name each amendment.

## Recovery

`orca orchestration run-list`, `orca orchestration run-use --id <run>`,
`orca orchestration worker-list --run <run> --json`, then `RUN/status.md` and the run files.

After an Orca restart an executor's terminal is gone while its dispatch may still be open
(liliiachaika plan 033). Read what it left: `git -C WT log -1 --format=%H%n%s`,
`git -C WT status --porcelain` and its progress file. `worker-release` the old dispatch, then
start a fresh executor (section 2, step 2) with a short spec: the commit or the uncommitted
files it inherits, the checklist items still open and the Acceptance to rerun. Never restart
the whole task over work that is already there, and never commit an executor's files yourself.
